proposals.before: In the eighth month of autumn, on the renwu day, the grand empress dowager deposed Emperor Fei as Prince of Jinan with the income of a single commandery, and installed the grand chief minister, Prince Yan of Changshan, as successor to the throne.
proposals.after: In the eighth month of autumn, on the renwu day, the grand empress dowager demoted Emperor Fei to Prince of Jinan with the income of a single commandery, and installed the grand chief minister, Prince Yan of Changshan, as successor to the throne.
proposals.reason: Chinese 廢帝爲濟南王 means demoting/deposing him to the status of Prince of Jinan, not “deposed … as” which reads as if “Prince of Jinan” were the office removed.

proposals.before: When his attendants asked why, the crown prince said, "This is where Shizong was killed; the Prince of Hejian has no place here."
proposals.after: When his attendants asked why, the crown prince said, "This is where Shizong met the assassins; why should the Prince of Hejian be here again?"
proposals.reason: Chinese 遇賊處 is “where he met the assassins/bandits,” and 復何宜在此 includes “again” (復); the idiomatic version over-translates to “killed” and drops 復.

decisions.reason: s0047’s 廢帝爲濟南王 means the grand empress dowager stripped him of the emperorship and made him Prince of Jinan. English “deposed … as Prince of Jinan” wrongly suggests Prince of Jinan was the office removed; “demoted … to Prince of Jinan” matches the Chinese construction.
世宗遇賊處 is the place where Shizong met the assassins/bandits, not an explicit “was killed,” and 復何宜在此 includes 復 “again.” The proposed wording restores both points without adding unstated content.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 世宗遇賊處，河間王復何宜在此
